consideredAndDeclined.item: Coordinator note rather than a finding: the live v2 appears to have received only one live independent review
consideredAndDeclined.observation: The dispatch and prompt state that the Codex v2 verdict measured the stale incomplete digest abdce147 and is not a finding against live v2, and v3's own basedOn records the same. I verified what I can: the v2 file on disk is 11a305c6 and abdce147 is not in the tree. I could not verify which digest the Codex verdict actually measured, because that would require opening the other reviewer's file, so that half rests on the coordinator's assertion and v3's recital.
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: It is not a defect in v3, which handles the situation transparently by pinning live v2 and disclaiming the stale verdict in its own bytes. I record it because a later act recording this lineage on dual independent ACCEPT should know that on the live v2 the dual review may have been effectively single, and may want the v2 cycle's standing stated explicitly in that entry.

consideredAndDeclined.item: Charging the permissive 'may use strace' phrasing as leaving the Linux mechanism optional
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: The permission is bounded on both sides: some mechanism is mandatory because absence of an observation mechanism fails the job and vacuous pass is a named fail condition, while strace is now lawful precisely because the child it traces is not a timing sample. Offering a permitted mechanism rather than mandating one specific tool is appropriate for a specification that must run on two platforms.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with no advisories. Fifteen attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: v3 at 175723e3 and frozen v2 at 11a305c6, both 0444 and unmoved, dispatch and prompt agreeing, HEAD never left 5d5d778, file 08 at 3a9442d1 equal to the subject's own pin, governing tree clean, and all five basedOn pins plus the file-08 pin reproduce. On the stale-write warning: the v2 file on disk hashes to the declared-live 11a305c6 and abdce147 is not in the tree, and v3 pins live v2 correctly while mentioning abdce147 exactly once, to disclaim the verdict taken against it. My finding landed in full and I verified it against D-102's own preflight paragraph rather than the disposition text. The no-load observation is now a dedicated launch of the same P+D in the hostile-fixture initial state, strace is lawful on Linux precisely because that child is not a timing sample, the macOS options are unchanged, and a new standingVsD102 field says the observation child is SIGKILLed and reaped matching D-102 preflight before quoting D-102's rule verbatim that timing samples proceed without ptrace or suspend. exactByteIntent now separates the 21 timing records from the one observation record per command, and three fail conditions were added covering observation on a timing sample, a ptraced or suspended timed child, and reading the specification as amending D-102 preflight. The repair does not weaken the test: both hostile fixtures, the initial state, the load definition and the missing-observation-is-a-fail rule are unchanged, so only the launch discipline moved. It is also surgical — DR-G03 alone changed, in three fields, with G01, G02, G04 and G05 byte-identical to v2, d006UnitStanding byte-identical, the byte constants still confined to refusals, and OBL-2 still not closed. One note for you rather than a finding: the dispatch, the prompt and v3 all record that the Codex v2 verdict measured the stale abdce147 write. I verified the parts I can — live v2 is 11a305c6 and abdce147 is absent — but I did not open the Codex verdict to confirm which digest it measured, because independence outranks settling it. If that is right, the live v2 had one live reviewer, and a later act recording this lineage on dual independent ACCEPT may want the v2 cycle's standing stated explicitly.
